assessment:
Four wishes. Four cards in the 99 search the library for something other than a land, enumerated over all 98 entries by oracle text: Vampiric Tutor ({B}, instant, any card, on top, you lose 2), Demonic Tutor ({1}{B}, sorcery, any card, to hand), Enlightened Tutor ({W}, instant, an artifact or enchantment card, revealed, on top) and Diabolic Intent ({1}{B}, sorcery, any card, to hand, sacrifice a creature as an additional cost). The five fetch lands search for lands and Path to Exile hands its search to the creature's controller; neither is a wish. deck-audit's tutors axis reads 4.

What they are for. The game ends when a loss-to-gain half (Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Exquisite Blood) sits beside a gain-to-loss half (Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose; Sanguine Bond; Enduring Tenacity; Marauding Blight-Priest) and anything gains you life. Three pairings are fact and all three run through Conqueror: stack 004 with Vito, 006 with Sanguine Bond, 012 with Tenacity. Each is deterministic, shortcut-legal, costs no mana, kills the table from any nonzero gain and carries on when a seat dies mid-loop. The Exquisite Blood pairings passed the checker on older boards (001 with Vito, 005 with Bond) and engine.json withholds them until a current board is re-run; the Blight-Priest pairings have no stack. A pair is drawn in 22.1% of games unassisted and 10.8% by turn six (mean turn 5.98); with a tutor, 57.3% and 33.3% (mean 5.653) (goldfish, seed 42, 10,000 games, model b025d0102196, decklist a872115f). That 35-point gap is these four cards, and the assisted column credits them together, so no figure here is one tutor's own.

Where not to point them. Six components are above 60% unassisted: a castable Vampire 84.9%, ramp 75.8%, a draw engine 75.2%, a free outlet 69.1%, protection 60.6%, a death drain 60.4%. Three are not: a token multiplier 37.1%, the noncreature answer 20.3% (one card, Anguished Unmaking, 66.6% assisted, the widest assisted gap in the artifact), Bloodletter with Sanctum Seeker 4.5%. The wishes below point at the loop, at the three thin components, and at four cards for boards where the loop is the wrong card: Anguished Unmaking, Teferi's Protection, Olivia's Wrath, Liliana, Dreadhorde General.

Which half. With a converter out the fetch is Conqueror; nothing else on the fact tier closes. With Conqueror out, the converter is a choice of three verified cards and the choice is what the table has shown: Vito costs {2}{B} and is a 1/3; Sanguine Bond costs {3}{B}{B} and is never a creature; Enduring Tenacity costs {2}{B}{B} and comes back as an enchantment when it is destroyed or shrunk to death (stack 012). Destroy shown: Tenacity. Exile or bounce shown: Bond. Five mana and a tapped-out table: Vito.

Timing. Vampiric and Enlightened put the card on top, so cast them at the end step of the player to your right or in your own upkeep; the card is then this turn's draw. Demonic and Intent put it in hand on your main phase, and the fetched card can be cast the same turn when the mana is there: Demonic or Intent plus Vito is five, plus Tenacity six, plus Bond or Conqueror seven. Mean available mana reads 5.323 on turn five, 6.045 on six, 6.73 on seven, 7.454 on eight. Intent is also a death: its cost fires Cruel Celebrant, Vraan, Blood Artist and Vein Ripper before the search resolves, and with Conqueror out those drains are gains.

The life. Vampiric costs 2, Anguished Unmaking 3, and the painlands and Talismans bill you every turn. Pay freely while every seat is above 25. Stop the turn a drain seat or a pinger has you in range: log 005 was lost to pings on an older list.

tutors.notes: {B}, instant, any card, on top, 2 life, and your next draw is the card. It reveals nothing. Four rules. (1) Cast it at the end step of the player to your right or in your own upkeep, never earlier: a card on top for a full round is a card the table has a round to answer. (2) Cast it only when you will cast the fetched card the turn it arrives; count that mana now. (3) Never buy what the deck already finds; the six components above 60% are not what this card is for. (4) Read the black. 37 black sources against a Karsten target of 36, black on curve 0.916 with rocks (mana_analysis), and the casts most worth buying are {3}{B}{B} (Conqueror, Bond), {2}{B}{B} (Tenacity) and {1}{B}{B}{B} (Bloodletter). Master of Dark Rites pays the creature ones: tap and sacrifice another creature for {B}{B}{B}, spendable on Vampire, Cleric and Demon spells. Conqueror is a Vampire Knight, Vito a Vampire Cleric, Bloodletter a Vampire Demon; Tenacity is a Snake Glimmer and Bond is an enchantment, and the Rites pay neither. One line nobody measures: with Twilight Prophet out and the city's blessing, the card you put on top is revealed in your upkeep, goes to your hand, and drains each opponent its mana value. Conqueror is 5. goldfish meta lists Prophet under drain_not_modelled and no stack walks it.

targets.why:
Conqueror is the only loss-to-gain half on the fact tier (004, 006 and 012 all run through him; the Exquisite Blood stacks are withheld), and with Vito out the pair is stack 004: Vito drains, Conqueror gains it back, Vito triggers again, each trigger aimed afresh, and the chain crosses a seat's death. The seed is already on your board. Sacrifice a token to Viscera Seer: Celebrant gains you 1, Vito drains 1 from the seat you name, Conqueror gains 1. The triggers are mandatory, so once Conqueror resolves the next death is the game. From a 1-life seed the seat at 14 takes 14 iterations; the stack proves the walk, not this board's count.

Rates: a pair drawn in 22.1% of games unassisted, 57.3% assisted; 10.8% by turn six against 33.3%; mean turn 5.98 against 5.653. The assisted figures credit all four tutors together.

The price is the seat at 27. Four open for two turns and nothing cast is a held instant in this model, and Conqueror is a 5/5 creature: stack 004 names every iteration's priority window as a window for creature removal. So the fetch is right now and the cast is not yet. Cast him the turn you also hold Deflecting Swat or Flawless Maneuver with Edgar on the battlefield, or the turn that seat taps below two. strategic_frame.json reads the free clause as needing Edgar on the battlefield, not in the command zone, and no stack has settled that; with Edgar in the zone, count both spells at full price. Teferi's Protection is not cover here: it phases out your own loop. The assumption stated: four open twice is removal. If it is a counterspell, a tutor at the end step gave it nothing to see.

A triggered ability is targeted if it identifies something it will affect by using the phrase “target [something],” where the “something” is a phrase that describes an object and/or player. The target(s) are chosen as the ability is put on the stack; see rule 603.3d.

Occasionally the game gets into a state in which a set of actions could be repeated indefinitely (thus creating a “loop”). In that case, the shortcut rules can be used to determine how many times those actions are repeated without having to actually perform them, and how the loop is broken.

targets.why:
Three converters are verified beside Conqueror and this board picks Tenacity. Stack 012 walks it: from a 2-life seed, 6 resolutions kill a seat at 12 and 15 more kill a seat at 30, each trigger aimed afresh, and the difference from Vito (004) and Bond (006) is what happens when the table shoots the converter. Destroy or -X/-X on Tenacity puts it in the graveyard as a creature; its own trigger returns it as an enchantment with the drain sentence intact, and the loop does not pause. The stack lists what does break that half: exile, bounce, a countered return trigger, enchantment removal after the return, or any removal on Conqueror. The mono-black seat's two destroy effects are the signal: against that seat, Tenacity is the converter that does not stay dead.

Why not Sanguine Bond: {3}{B}{B} against {2}{B}{B}, and against destroy both are safe. Fetch Bond instead when a seat shows exile or bounce, which takes Tenacity for good and Bond only with an enchantment answer. Why not Vito: cheapest at {2}{B}, and a 1/3 that dies to everything this table has shown. Mean mana on turn seven reads 6.73; Tenacity leaves three open, enough for Flawless Maneuver at full price if Edgar is not out.

The seed: Blood Artist gains you 1 on any creature's death, theirs included, so with Tenacity resolved the next death anywhere starts the loop. Name the seat before the first trigger resolves; the target is chosen per iteration, and a gain of 0 is not a gain.

targets.why:
Fetch the answer, not the threat. Anguished Unmaking is the one card in the 99 that exiles any nonland permanent, enumerated over deck-audit's interaction axis: Path to Exile and Elspeth's -3 need a creature, Vish Kal's counters and Erebos's -2/-1 need a creature, Olivia's Wrath reads non-Vampire creatures, Anowon and Liliana are edicts, Deflecting Swat retargets. The noncreature-answer component is 20.3% drawn and 13.3% by turn six; 66.6% and 48.6% assisted, the widest assisted gap the goldfish reports, and it is this one card. A tutor at the end step reveals nothing; Unmaking is drawn on your turn and held as an instant with three open.

Against a combo seat the held answer rots. The last profitable moment is the half you can see, before the second one lands: exile it at their upkeep, or in response to the second half's cast if you can see it coming. Life: Unmaking costs 3 and the tutor 2, and at 34 against a table above 30 that is currency.

Teferi's Protection is the other card this tutor could buy: it stops your life total changing until your next turn and does nothing to the piece, so it buys one turn and Unmaking buys the game. The assumption stated: their end-step tutor fetched the second half. If it fetched mana, Unmaking still exiles the half on board and the loop you fear is one card further away.

Stack 003 is this arithmetic. Seven attacking Vampires give seven Sanctum Seeker triggers; on your turn Bloodletter's replacement doubles each opponent's loss, so each seat loses 14 before blockers are declared and the seat at 14 is dead by state-based actions. Your own gain is not doubled: the text replaces an opponent's loss only. Count them again without him: six attackers is 12 a seat and the seat at 14 lives on 2.

The loop is off the table on this board, so this is the route. Its measured component, Bloodletter with Sanctum Seeker, is 4.5% assembled, 1.9% by turn six, mean turn 6.462; 33.0% and 15.9% assisted. targets.why:
The tax is the piece that beats you, not the scariest piece. Twenty-three nonland entries at mana value two or less are this deck's speed, and {1} on each is half their cost; Urza's Incubator counters it for Vampire creature spells only. The outs, enumerated: Anguished Unmaking is the one card in the 99 that exiles a noncreature permanent; Deflecting Swat retargets, Path and the edicts need creatures, Olivia's Wrath reads non-Vampire creatures. deck-audit reads interaction breadth at three of five classes, artifact covered by this one copy; 7.1% of opening sevens hold it; the component is 20.3% drawn, 66.6% assisted.

Seven mana under the tax is Demonic at three and Unmaking at four in one turn: the tax leaves with the spell that paid for it, and the two Vampires in hand cost their printed price next turn. Three life, at 29 against a 6-power clock: the last cheap points. If the tax seat has fewer than two open, cast both now. If they hold two, cast the tutor and keep Unmaking as an instant for their end step: it is the only spell in the line a counter needs to hit.

The assumption stated: the tax seat is not the beatdown; the Rakdos seat is, and under the tax you are racing them too, which is why the out comes before the Vampires in hand.

Liliana: whenever a creature you control dies, draw a card; +1 makes a 2/2; -4 makes each player sacrifice two. Eight mana is Intent at two and Liliana at six in one turn. Pay the Intent with Bloodghast: it returns on your next land drop, and because Liliana is still in the library when the cost is paid, that death draws nothing. Sequence Intent first, Liliana second, and every later death is a card: tokens into an outlet, Bloodghast every turn, the -4 as four deaths across the table.

Flawless Maneuver covers him if Edgar is out; with Edgar in the zone it costs {2}{W} you do not have this turn, so the honest line is Conqueror next turn with three open, or now if the seat taps below two.
